notes.meaning: The Lord tells Moses to give the Israelites the exact borders of the land they will receive. Canaan is described as an inheritance, meaning it is a gift from God rather than something earned. By setting strict boundaries, God assures them of victory while warning them not to push beyond these limits in greedy conquest.

The southern border starts at the bottom tip of the Salt Sea, also known as the Dead Sea. It winds south of the steep cliffs of Akrabbim, passes Kadesh-barnea, and follows the Brook of Egypt out to the Mediterranean Sea. These rugged valleys and desert lands formed a natural wall of protection along Israel's southern frontier.

The Great Sea, which is called the Mediterranean Sea today, marks the entire western border of the land. It is called great to separate it from the smaller inland lakes found in the region. This wide coastline gave Israel a clear and natural boundary along the west.

The northern border begins at the Mediterranean Sea and climbs toward a high peak called Mount Hor in the Lebanon range. It then reaches past the entrance of Hamath and travels through northern towns until it ends at Hazar-enan. This line kept Israel separated from the foreign nations living to the far north.

The eastern boundary runs south from Hazar-enan through Shepham and down along the slopes east of the Sea of Chinnereth, which is the Sea of Galilee. From there, the border follows the Jordan River all the way down to the Salt Sea. This placed the river and the lakes inside the care of the tribes living on the western side.

Moses instructs the people that this outlined territory must be divided by lot among nine and a half tribes. Casting lots allowed God Himself to decide where each family would live, which prevented fighting and jealousy. God wanted each tribe to be content with the specific portion He provided for them.

The tribes of Reuben and Gad, along with half the tribe of Manasseh, had already received their territory east of the Jordan River. Because they asked for and accepted the conquered lands opposite Jericho, they were not included in this new western distribution. Their earlier settlement was officially confirmed so that everyone knew their proper place.

The Lord names Eleazar the priest and Joshua to lead the distribution, along with one chief from each remaining tribe. Appointing these leaders before the fighting even started showed complete trust that God would give them the land. Having a trusted prince from every tribe guaranteed that the land would be handed out fairly and peacefully.

Caleb is named first to represent the tribe of Judah, followed by Shemuel for Simeon and Elidad for Benjamin. Caleb had faithfully trusted God's promise forty years earlier, and now he is chosen to help claim the prize. These three tribes would end up living close together in the southern portion of the country.

Leaders are appointed for Dan, Manasseh, and Ephraim: Bukki, Hanniel, and Kemuel. Manasseh and Ephraim, the descendants of Joseph, are placed side by side just as they would settle in the land. God arranged these leaders in the exact neighborhood where their families would later live.

Eli-zaphan is chosen for the tribe of Zebulun, and Paltiel is chosen for the tribe of Issachar. These two tribes were descended from the same mother, Leah, and would receive neighboring parcels in the northern part of the country. God paired them together for mutual support and peaceful living.

The last two leaders chosen are Ahihud from the tribe of Asher and Pedahel from the tribe of Naphtali. These two tribes would settle side by side in the farthest northern section of Canaan. Listing them last matched the northern edge of the map where their inheritance would lie.

God commanded these specific men to distribute the inheritance across Canaan for the whole nation. Choosing them by name gave divine authority to the final division, so no one could question their decisions. It assured Israel that their future homes were arranged under God's watchful care.
